# Agent Architectures

[Home](../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../README.md) · [简体中文](agent-architectures_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Agent Architectures

Architectures organizing Agents for dexterous semantic understanding/data annotation or runtime planning and execution. Specify the Agent stage, inter-module interfaces, reasoning/memory responsibilities and actual grasp generator or controller. Distinguish annotation from online control and low-level switching from high-level replanning. Agent collaboration must be a substantive contribution; incidental Agent use does not determine placement. Task planning, skill composition and recovery remain visible tags.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.2] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-2"></a> | **AdaClearGrasp｜Adaptive clearing · RL dexterous grasping · Failure replanning**<br>[AdaClearGrasp: Learning Adaptive Clearing for Zero-Shot Robust Dexterous Grasping in Densely Cluttered Environments](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.10616v1)<br>Zixuan Chen, Wenquan Zhang, Jing Fang, Ruiming Zeng, Zhixuan Xu, Yiwen Hou, Xinke Wang, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `task-planning` `adaptive-clearing` `cluttered-grasping` `skill-library` `model-context-protocol` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `geometry-aware-policy` `failure-recovery` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | AdaClearGrasp uses a VLM to choose direct grasping or push/pull clearing from the scene and execution feedback, invokes geometric planning skills and a PPO-trained GeoGrasp policy through MCP, and replans after failures to grasp targets in dense clutter.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct planner emits tool calls and parameters; geometric planners execute clearing/reset skills, and failure reports change subsequent skill selection. GeoGrasp is a PPO-trained MLP with 59-D observations: normalized nearest-point vectors from 18 hand keypoints, target height, and TCP height/orientation. Christensen, Haozhi Qi<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `affordance-reasoning` `future-aware-planning` `object-centric-control` `object-trajectory-interface` `reach-acquire-move` `skill-composition` `reusable-contact-primitive` `cross-embodiment` `cross-hand-transfer` `canonical-link-joint-representation` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [contact-estimation](../../topics/tactile.md) `pose-feedback-tracking` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | GOTT interfaces through desired object trajectories and reach specifications: a VLM selects task-relevant contact regions, planning and IK select feasible approaches, a shared cross-hand PPO primitive establishes stable contact in closed loop, and a pose-feedback tracker executes the object motion, reusing contact skills across tasks, arms and hands.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Default VLM affordance selection and full-trajectory IK checks generate reaches; demonstrations/external models can also supply specifications. Acquire uses a PPO-trained MLP with local hand–object geometry and proprioceptive history to output wrist/finger deltas. A contact predictor triggers Move after sustained thumb-plus-finger contact; Move is geometric pose-feedback tracking, not RL. Unseen-Allegro-variant zero-shot results are simulated. Planning and acquisition run sequentially; phase switching does not establish high-level feedback replanning. | [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.5] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-5"></a> | **ZeroDex｜Multi-view 3D grounding · Tool trajectory transfer · Closed-loop replanning**<br>[ZeroDex: Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation via Multi-View 3D-Grounded VLM Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.19340v2)<br>Jisoo Kim, Sangwon Baik, Taeksoo Kim, Sungjoo Kim, Junyoung Lee, Mingi Choi, Hanbyul Joo<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `multi-view-3d-grounding` `robust-triangulation` `reference-view-ray-voting` `affordance-grounding` `tool-use` `object-centric-atomic-actions` `tool-trajectory-alignment` `grasp-optimization` `inverse-kinematics` `collision-aware-motion-planning` `task-planning` `closed-loop-verification` `failure-replanning` `zero-shot-manipulation` `real-world` | ZeroDex lifts VLM-grounded 2D functional keypoints into 3D using multi-view triangulation and reference-ray voting, aligns stored tool trajectories, optimizes grasps and plans arm–hand motions, then uses visual verification and replanning for zero-shot long-horizon manipulation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A VLM decomposes tasks and identifies grasp, interaction and terminal points. When cross-view triangulation lacks consensus, other views vote over depth candidates on the reference ray. Skill-category retrieval supplies offline recorded/generated 6D tool trajectories aligned to the scene; affordance-constrained grasps and motion planning undergo full-trajectory IK/collision checks. Post-execution decisions continue, re-ground and retry, or replace the subtask plan. No task-specific policy training is required, but pretrained perception, an offline skill library and motion planning are used, rather than VLA action generation. Hardware uses xArm + Inspire with 4–6 calibrated RGB cameras, FoundationStereo depth and FoundationPose poses. Long-horizon organization scores 4/6 and cooking 1/3, including recovery within a retry budget of four; other tasks typically have 5 or 10 trials, not broad evidence of reliable long-horizon performance. In-hand reorientation is unsupported. The project provides demonstrations; code remains marked coming soon at verification. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.19340v2) · [Project](https://jlogkim.github.io/zerodex/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.7] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-7"></a> | **LUCID｜Closed-loop intent prediction · Human video learning · Generalist arm-hand control**<br>[LUCID: Learning Embodiment-Agnostic Intent Models from Unstructured Human Videos for Scalable Dexterous Robot Skill Acquisition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.11628v1)<br>Harsh Gupta, Guanya Shi, Wenzhen Yuan<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `parallel-jaw-gripper` `agent-architecture` `intent-control-separation` `closed-loop-intent-prediction` `human-video-learning` `object-flow` `palm-pose-reference` `goal-conditioned-policy` `task-agnostic-controller` `cross-embodiment` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `teacher-student-distillation` `procedural-reference-generation` `eigen-grasps` `per-joint-hand-residuals` `wrist-depth` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | LUCID learns closed-loop object-point and palm-pose trajectory prediction from human video, then uses a generalist arm–hand policy trained in procedural simulation to turn these references and live observations into arm-joint increments and coordinated grasp motions plus finger residuals, linking different embodiments through a shared intent interface.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Interface: two recent RGB-D frames, 16 current 3D object query points and current palm pose produce an eight-step, one-second object-point/palm reference R at 1 Hz. The student consumes R, live points, wrist depth and proprioceptive/action history; point/depth tokens are read by proprioception-conditioned attention and an MLP. Its 50-Hz, 27-D output comprises six arm-joint increments, five grasp coefficients and 16 finger residuals. Hand increments are E times coefficients plus residuals, with E a five-component PCA basis of retargeted human grasps. Increments accumulate on previous joint targets and undergo smoothing/clipping before PD control; palm references condition the network rather than being added as wrist base actions. Intent models train per task on human video. Independently, procedural objects/references train a PPO teacher with privileged state, then a deployable student with PPO plus action distillation and camera/proprioceptive observations. Deployment updates references/actions without weight updates. A task-agnostic controller is reused within each embodiment; intent transfers across embodiments while controllers train separately. LEAP stirring, wiping and binning each use about 20k web clips; Push-T and cable routing each use one hour of smartphone video and are evaluated with hand/gripper controllers. Stirring needs an external stop; occlusion and unstable grasps remain failure modes. The project presents methods/examples; code, data and pretrained-weight availability is unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.11628v1) · [Project](https://lucid-robot.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |

DINOv3 and trained Contact-GraspNet supply candidates; a Seed-1.8 Agent uses taxonomy retrieval and stepwise reasoning, with SAM3 grounding objects/parts. Hand-specific lookup/kinematics yields wrist poses and joints; a shared PointTransformer scores contact points/normals using BCE on simulated outcomes, without RL. Its 4.4 million training trials cover DH3, Allegro and Inspire; new hands still need mapping tables. Dynamic execution rigidly transforms the initial wrist pose, retaining joints and bypassing renewed scoring, rather than invoking per-frame Agent replanning. Hardware includes ROHand and parallel grippers. Static ROHand functional grasping achieves 83.3% over 510 trials on 102 objects; dynamic updates run at 5 Hz. Validation concerns single-step functional grasping, without complete subsequent tool use or tactile correction. Code, training-data and pretrained-weight availability remains unverified. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04096v2) · [Project](https://adarobovlg.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |

| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.3] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-3"></a> | **DexGraspVLA｜Hierarchical VLA · Domain-invariant visual representations · Diffusion imitation learning**<br>[DexGraspVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Framework Towards General Dexterous Grasping](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.20900v5)<br>Yifan Zhong, Xuchuan Huang, Ruochong Li, Ceyao Zhang, Zhang Chen, Tianrui Guan, Fanlian Zeng, Ka Nam Lui, Yuyao Ye, Yitao Liang, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` [vla](../../topics/vla.md) `vlm` `task-planning` `visual-grounding` `object-mask-tracking` `domain-invariant-representation` `dinov2` `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `action-chunking` `failure-recovery` `real-world` | DexGraspVLA uses a VLM to select successive grasp targets and bounding boxes, converts them into tracked masks with SAM/Cutie, and combines these with frozen DINOv2 features to guide a demonstration-trained diffusion arm-hand policy; the planner checks execution and selects the next target, while stable intermediate representations support generalization across objects, lighting and backgrounds.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Runtime target selection and outcome monitoring coordinate closed-loop execution. | [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.6] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-6"></a> | **VLM Scaffolding｜Keypoint trajectory planning · Residual RL · Sim-to-real**<br>[Scaffolding Dexterous Manipulation with Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.19212v3)<br>Vincent de Bakker, Joey Hejna, Tyler Ga Wei Lum, Onur Celik, Aleksandar Taranovic, Denis Blessing, Gerhard Neumann, Jeannette Bohg, Dorsa Sadigh<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `hierarchical-planning-control` `keypoint-trajectory-planning` `semantic-keypoints` `trajectory-scaffolding` `task-planning` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `plan-conditioned-policy` `keypoint-tracking-reward` `demonstration-free` `in-context-learning` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | VLM Scaffolding generates coarse object-keypoint and wrist trajectories from images and instructions, using them as reward targets and action references to train a residual RL policy in simulation; the policy then corrects wrist motion and controls fingers using live keypoint feedback.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Gemini 2.5 Flash Thinking detects semantic 2D points, lifts them using calibrated RGB-D, and generates interpolated keypoint/wrist plans. Each task uses 100 initial-state/plan pairs to train a three-layer MLP with PPO. Rewards combine object-keypoint tracking and contact count; wrist plans instead serve as bounded-residual action references. Test-time plans condition a frozen policy on proprioception, tracked keypoints and future plans. FoundationPose supplies hardware keypoints; execution feedback acts at the low level, while successful plans improve subsequent VLM prompts without online weight updates. Human demonstrations are unnecessary, but task prompts, simulation scenes and generic tracking/contact rewards remain. Eight Allegro simulation tasks mostly use whole-hand opening/closing; scissors/pliers use one control per finger, not per joint. KUKA LBR iiwa 14 + 16-DoF Allegro hardware achieves 90% bottle placement, 85% box pushing and 65% triple hammering over 20 trials per task (four plans repeated five times), using digital twins and domain randomization. Official plan-generation, RL-training and hardware code is public; pretrained-policy weight availability is unverified. | arXiv v3 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.19212v3) · [Project](https://sites.google.com/view/vlm-scaffolding/home) · [Code](https://github.com/vdebakker/vlm-scaffolding) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.8] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-8"></a> | **OmniDexVLG｜Multi-Agent semantic understanding and annotation · VLG grasp generation · Fine-grained grasp control**<br>[OmniDexVLG: Learning Dexterous Grasp Generation from Vision Language Model-Guided Grasp Semantics, Taxonomy and Functional Affordance](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.03874v1)<br>Lei Zhang, Diwen Zheng, Kaixin Bai, Zhenshan Bing, Zoltán-Csaba Márton, Zhaopeng Chen, Alois Christian Knoll, Jianwei Zhang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent` `agent-architecture` `multi-agent` `training-data-annotation` `semantic-reasoning` `retrieval-augmented-generation` `chain-of-thought` `grasp-taxonomy` `contact-semantics` `functional-affordance` `language-conditioned-grasping` `vision-language-grasping` `conditional-diffusion` `partial-point-cloud` `synthetic-grasp-data` `differentiable-force-closure` `leap-hand` `dlr-hit-ii` `real-world` | OmniDexVLG uses collaborating Agents to interpret hand–object contacts, infer grasp types and generate language annotations, then trains point-cloud/language-conditioned diffusion to control grasp regions, participating fingers and grasp types.<br>**Evaluation scope:** DataGen samples and physically validates taxonomy/contact/affordance-aware grasps. Reasoner combines multiview images, hand configurations and contacts with multi-Agent reasoning, retrieval and stepwise inference to annotate data. GraspNet generates target poses from partial point clouds and instructions. The three modules are not three Agents: Agent contributions concern semantic understanding/annotation, without demonstrated online Agent replanning or RL action learning. PyRoki plans hardware trajectories for impedance control. Data generation/reasoning involve LEAP and DLR-HIT II; the final generator is evaluated only with LEAP in simulation and on a Diana arm, not as a unified cross-hand model. Outputs are poses, not continuous manipulation trajectories. Project access is verified; code, data and pretrained downloads are not. | arXiv v1 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.03874v1) · [Project](https://sites.google.com/view/omnidexvlg) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
